sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

stage_1.expense_line_item: NUANS name search report and preliminary name clearance for the proposed ULC name
stage_1.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS service provider
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately CAD 25 for a standard NUANS report, plus nominal agent handling fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; sections 12, 23, 24, 101, 118, 121, and Part 16.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporations), including sections 252.1-252.5.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry Division)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The unlimited liability corporation may issue shares for such consideration as the board determines; no escrow, capitalization deposit, or proof of funds is required at incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription for the issued shares of the corporation be and is hereby approved, and the shares listed in the subscription record be issued to the proposed subscriber upon receipt of payment in full, whether cash, cleared wire, or acceptable property. RESOLVED that the registered office of the corporation be established at the address stated in the Notice of Registered Office, and that the named registered agent shall remain the agent for service of process in Alberta. RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed as officers of the corporation: President, Secretary and Treasurer, each with authority to execute contracts and banking documents incidental to the corporation's business. RESOLVED that the officers execute and deliver all certificates, notices, and filings required under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request through the Alberta Corporate Registry e-filing system or an authorized service provider to verify that the proposed unlimited liability corporation name is distinct and compliant with Alberta name rules. If approved, reserve the name for the permitted statutory period.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or non-distinctive, submit a revised name accompanied by a new name search report and pay the applicable reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles and Organizational Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered solicitor or notary in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation including the unlimited liability corporation designation, authorized share structure, registered office location, first directors, and permitted restrictions on business. Draft Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and consents to act as directors and officers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If internal filing checks identify defects, revise the articles and notices before formal submission to avoid registry rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) e-filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office, and Notice of Directors through the Alberta Corporate Registry online system. Pay the prescribed filing fee and wait for the registry to issue the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or rejection notice, cure the stated deficiency within the prescribed period, resubmit the corrected instrument electronically, and pay any resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and Initial Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Unlimited Liability Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, approve share subscription and issuance, confirm the registered office and registered agent, appoint officers, approve corporate banking resolutions, and adopt the corporate minute book and share certificate form.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer declines appointment, execute a replacement consent and amend the board resolution before issuing shares or opening bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Tax Authorities and Provincial Administrative Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated entity with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a Business Number, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and any required payroll account if the company will have employees. Confirm Alberta provincial tax registration requirements and update all government records with the registered office and directors.
required_dossiers: CRA RC1 request for Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is refused or the Business Number is delayed, verify the corporate status with Alberta Corporate Registry and resubmit the registration request through CRA Business Registration Online or contact the CRA Business Enquiries line.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; ancillary municipal business licensing through the applicable Alberta municipality if warehousing or storage premises are used
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no provincial operating license is required for wholesale remarketing and trading of used construction excavators under ISIC 4659 / NAICS 423810

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or exemption in relation to storage and wholesale handling of used heavy machinery; full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not ordinarily required unless land disturbance, waste storage, or contaminated materials handling exceeds regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance required with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and applicable wastewater discharge limits under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act and Alberta Water Act. Stormwater runoff from storage yards must not contain free petroleum hydrocarbons; oil, coolant, and hydraulic fluid must be contained and disposed of as hazardous waste. Volatile organic compound emissions are not significant from static storage but any degreasing or repair activity must meet air emissions standards and fugitive VOC limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code, including storage-area fire separation and extinguisher placement; structural load inspection for any racking, platforms, or mezzanines used in machinery storage; and occupational health and safety clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, including traffic management, heavy-lift equipment inspection, lockout/tagout for equipment servicing, spill response, first aid, and workplace hazard communication standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll accounts; Albertan corporate registrations through Alberta Corporate Registry and extra-provincial licensing by Corporations Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned entity must obtain a federal GST/HST account by registering with CRA (Form RC1 or online via My Business Account), providing Canadian business address, anticipated Canadian revenues, and appointed authorized representative; if carrying on business in Alberta, file extra-provincial registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry; no separate Alberta income tax return for ULC beyond the general federal/provincial coordination.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No full Canadian check-the-box regime; CRA may respect a foreign corporation's pass-through classification for Canadian tax purposes in limited treaty/non-resident circumstances. Available elections include section 256.1(1) and (2) of the Income Tax Act for treating an entity as a corporation or partnership, section 18(1) hybrid mismatch provisions under the MLI, and provincial attribution elections for Alberta corporate allocation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); no Alberta Provincial Sales Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD Canadian taxable revenue over any four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration available for foreign suppliers and exporters
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory national e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance in Canada; CRA accepts electronic invoices and records under GST/HST section 286 compliance. GST/HST returns are filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or Canada Revenue Agency business portal; no digital stamping or API tax clearance mandate applies in Alberta.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export supply applies to used construction excavators and heavy earthmoving equipment sold for export when title and possession transfer to a non-resident and the goods are exported as part of an arrangement; storage, freight, and export-related services may also be zero-rated if exported. The supplier must hold proof of export and commercial records evidencing the foreign destination.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny the zero-rating and assess unreported GST/HST, impose a clawback of any refund claimed, levy a 25% penalty on false statements or omission under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act, and charge interest from the original due date. Egregious repeat offenders face gross negligence penalties of 50% of tax owing and criminal prosecution under criminal tax evasion provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential oversight of payment and clearing systems executed by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and AML/ATF reporting to the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full free-float convertibility without exchange control restrictions. Canada imposes no capital account controls, no licensing of inward direct investment for wholesale trading (Investment Canada Act notification-only below jurisdictional review thresholds, and a greenfield Alberta ULC is not a reviewable acquisition), and no restrictions on CAD repatriation of dividends, interest, intercompany loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. A Canadian-resident ULC is a treaty-eligible resident under Article IV of the Canada-US Tax Treaty; Part XIII non-resident withholding on dividends is generally reduced under Article X (5% for a US corporate beneficial owner holding 10% or more voting rights, 15% portfolio), and arm's-length interest is exempt under Article XI. No sovereign approval is required to hold USD or EUR operating balances, and CAD weakness is market-determined only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Under the Currency Act and the PCMLTFA framework, Canadian law prohibits any mandatory surrender, conversion, or channeling of export proceeds; there is no statutory timeline and no conversion ratio applicable to exporters. The Alberta ULC exporting secondhand hydraulic earthmovers (HS 8429.52 / NAICS 423810) may retain 100% of USD/EUR proceeds in any convertible offshore or domestic foreign-currency account without Bank of Canada approval. The only compliance obligations are: (i) bank-filed FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report for each international EFT over CAD 10,000 remitted to the Minister within 5 business days; (ii) retention of the B13A export declaration, commercial invoice, and proof-of-payment reconciliation for the 6-year CRA record-retention window under ITA 230(1); and (iii) normal accrual of the realized or unrealized FX gain/loss for corporate income tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for settlement-critical wire and LC flows; Medium only as ancillary collection/FX conversion rails. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK EMI license class; fintechs (Wise Canada, Payoneer, Knightsbridge) operate as FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs) under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), without Schedule I Bank Act deposit-taking authority, CDIC insurance, SWIFT MT700 issuing capability, or direct CHIPS/Fedwire clearing. They may be used for sub-CAD 100,000 expense payments and small USD collection sweeps, but cannot serve as the primary treasury account for the CAD 500,000 to CAD 5,000,000 per-transaction used-excavator settlement profile. An offshore EMI (e.g., UK EMD or EU EMI) may not lawfully market deposit accounts into Canada absent a Representative Office or Schedule I license under the Bank Act and would additionally breach FINTRAC MSB registration requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch presence is not statutorily compulsory, but all Schedule I banks effectively require at least one director, the ULC's authorized officer, or a Power-of-Attorney signatory to complete an in-person or video-conference KYC interview before account activation. RBC, TD, and CIBC permit remote video notarization of the UBO and authorized signatories subject to certified passport, notarized corporate authorization resolution, and a physical Alberta registered-office address for banking-match purposes. A non-resident sole shareholder of the ULC must additionally present certificate of good standing from the home registry dated within 90 days, and OSFI guidance effectively mandates face-to-face or equivalent interview with the individual ultimate beneficial owner before onboarding a non-resident-owned corporate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident-owned Alberta ULC with no domestic payroll, no GST account, and no physical asset presence in Alberta (commercial substance red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate plus Certificate of Good Standing; Articles of Incorporation and ULC operating agreement reflecting the unlimited liability election; CRA Business Number and GST/HST account (RT0001) confirmation; 12-month projected financial statements with cash-flow forecast; Alberta warehouse or dealer-office lease agreement with utility bill; UBO passport and notarized source-of-wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-route sanctions and dual-use screening: HS 8429.52 excavator resales involving foreign auction houses, non-OECD buyers, or ambiguous end users (Russia/Belarus/Iran/North Korea screening flags)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada Export Control List (ECL) determination confirming no controlled item; OSFI/UN consolidated sanctions and OFAC SDN screening log with algorithmic matching of all counterparties, UBOs, and related brokers; notarized End-User/End-Use Certificate; equipment serial-number provenance report; transaction-specific exclusion letter confirming no brokering to sanctioned persons; signed compliance manual with escalation protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity wire settlements: expected monthly supplier disbursements aggregating above CAD 2.5 million across repetitive beneficiary structures (structuring/typology flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CPA-reviewed or audited 2-year financial statements of the ULC and, where material, its parent; executed master framework trade contracts incorporating Incoterms 2020; 12-month detailed cash-flow forecast filed with the bank; ULC board resolution establishing treasury committee authority and dual-approval mandates; 3-way matching package (invoice, inspection certificate, shipping documents) retained for the full 6-year period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP indicator arising from distributor counterparties or beneficial owners of trading partners in re-selling jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Enhanced Due Diligence Questionnaire (EDDQ) per PCMLTFA s. 11.1 for each PEP-linked entity; independent source-of-wealth report prepared by Canadian counsel or a licensed CPA; certified background/negative-media search report; board minute recording a FATF Recommendation 12 analysis and the continuous monitoring framework assigned to the designated compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing via SWIFT MT103 (USD via the Canadian bank's New York correspondent on CHIPS/Fedwire; CAD via Payments Canada Lynx/LVTS) using tag 70 purpose code 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION' for equity injection and 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN' for debt injection at an arm's-length rate to preserve Part XIII interest exemption under Article XI. Capital injections are not subject to mandatory FINTRAC reporting when executed through a Canadian bank (the bank reports all international EFTs over CAD 10,000 automatically), but the ULC must archive the bank credit advice, the board resolution authorizing the contribution, and the journal entry establishing contributed surplus or shareholder loan per ITA 230(1). First-inflow verification requires a certified true copy of the bank authorization resolution and a purpose declaration matching the KYC record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two-tier clearing architecture: (1) CAD domestic supplier payments settle in real time through Payments Canada Lynx (ISO 20022 pacs.008) with same-day finality; (2) USD/EUR cross-border trade disbursements execute by SWIFT MT103 with field 70/77B referencing the sales contract, HS 8429.52, and purchase-order number, cleared through the beneficiary bank's CHIPS/Fedwire membership. For fabrication, refurbishment, or auction-site settlements exceeding CAD 250,000, the blueprint mandates an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (Sight or Usance) issued under UCP600 with URR725 reimbursement terms, transmitted via SWIFT MT700/MT707 and confirmed by the advising bank. Standby Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT760/MT799) are reserved for performance and inspection guarantees during cross-border equipment handover.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with tenors up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the Canadian Master Agreement (CMARA), with collateral posted in a securities account of the Canadian bank

Vanilla FX Options (CAD/USD calls and puts) purchased OTC from the Schedule I bank dealing room, premiums payable in CAD, settled T+2, with counterparty credit embedded in the bank's trading authority matrix

Cross-Currency Swap (CAD/USD CCS) for matching long-dated USD equipment-acquisition liabilities against CAD operating cash flow, subject to OSFI Variation Margin (VM) rules under the ISDA Credit Support Annex

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on CNH/CAD (offshore RMB) where procurement from Asia-based used-equipment auction channels creates residual CNY exposure; permitted only as a cash-settlement instrument referenced to the Bank of Canada or Reuters CRS index and never involving a RUB-denominated or sanctioned counterparty contract
Multi-currency zero-balance account structure at one Schedule I bank enabling natural hedging of USD auction receipts against USD supplier disbursements with sub-account sweeps and no conversion cost

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return for Unlimited Liability Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in enforcement notices and continued delinquency; persistent non-filing can lead to administrative dissolution/strike-off by the Registrar, causing loss of corporate legal capacity and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (annual federal corporate tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Income Tax Act: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat non-compliance attracts 10% plus 2% per month; continued failure may trigger CRA collection enforcement and director liability assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue threshold under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); an independent auditor is required unless the corporation is not a reporting issuer and all shareholders unanimously resolve to waive the audit. Lenders or CRA may separately require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE for private Alberta ULCs unless shareholders, lenders, or CRA require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires ULCs to maintain an individuals with significant control (ISC) register and to update it within 30 days of any change, including share transfers. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members before filing the annual return; the annual return confirms current directors and registered office information with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–12,000 per year if audit is not waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate income tax rate: 15% federal plus 8% Alberta. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a combined 11% rate on up to CAD 500,000 of eligible active business income: 9% federal plus 2% Alberta, subject to business-limit and associated-corporation rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal and Alberta small-business deductions may reduce the rate for qualifying CCPCs. The federal general rate reduction, Alberta general corporate rate, capital cost allowance, accelerated investment incentive rules, immediate expensing rules where applicable, and ordinary business deductions may reduce taxable income. Canada generally has no broad corporate income tax holiday for an Alberta ULC. A ULC is ordinarily a corporation for Canadian tax purposes even if it is treated as fiscally transparent in another jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including applicable schedules, filed through CRA Corporation Internet Filing or authorized tax software. Alberta AT1 Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return and related schedules filed electronically through Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration NetFile or approved software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate tax instalments are generally monthly, or quarterly for eligible corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and AT1 are generally due six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance owing is generally payable two months after year-end, or three months after year-end for qualifying CCPCs meeting the statutory conditions. Instalment due dates apply during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, taxation year, province of permanent establishment, address, books-and-records location, and fiscal-period dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian legal entity's exact registered name and BN. Identify all Canadian permanent establishments and disclose foreign ownership, amalgamations, wind-ups, and changes in control where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related and associated corporations, ownership, control, business limits, and associated-CCPC information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent, affiliates, common-control entities, and associated corporations. Do not claim CCPC status unless the statutory Canadian-control requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income or loss to income for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible expenses, reconcile foreign exchange and accounting provisions, and separately identify tax adjustments for related-party transactions and capital items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance, fixed assets, depreciable classes, additions, dispositions, recapture, terminal losses, and shareholder information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify used excavators, rollers, inventory, and demonstration equipment correctly. Trading inventory is not depreciable capital property. Report controlling shareholders and ownership percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable federal tax-rate schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax calculation, general rate reduction, small-business deduction, refundable taxes, and applicable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled ULC normally cannot claim CCPC benefits. Test control, ownership, associated corporations, and business-limit allocation before claiming the small-business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident shareholder dividends, interest, and other distributions; foreign tax credits and related foreign income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, and other cross-border amounts with Part XIII withholding, NR4 slips, treaty positions, and general-ledger records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 29 or applicable federal investment-tax-credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal investment tax credits and other credits, if available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by eligible Canadian expenditures and required certificates. Used machinery trading income ordinarily does not create a general investment tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Alberta AT1 Taxable Income and Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income, permanent establishment allocation, Alberta tax rate, small-business deduction, credits, instalments, and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Alberta under applicable federal and Alberta allocation rules. Maintain evidence for Alberta employees, premises, inventory, sales functions, and management activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual reporting of material non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, including goods, services, financing, royalties, and transfers of property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File where the applicable aggregate transaction threshold is met, generally CAD 1 million for reportable categories, and retain transaction-level transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T1134 Information Return Relating to Controlled and Not-Controlled Foreign Affiliates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign affiliate ownership and income information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is generally relevant to Canadian-resident corporations with foreign affiliates, not merely because the ULC has foreign shareholders. Confirm filing status annually.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specified foreign property reporting for Canadian-resident corporations where the applicable cost threshold is exceeded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is not automatically a T1135 filer; analyze residence, property ownership, and excluded-property rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST/HST taxable supplies, input tax credits, adjustments, and net tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Used excavator sales, imports, exports, and interprovincial supplies require transaction-by-transaction place-of-supply analysis. Exported goods may be zero-rated if documentary conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: NR4 and Part XIII remittance records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts paid or credited to non-residents, withholding tax, remittances, and annual information slips.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold before or upon payment or credit, remit within the prescribed remittance period, issue NR4 slips, and retain treaty forms and beneficial-ownership evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing generally attracts a penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% of that balance for each complete month late, up to 12 months; higher repeated-failure penalties may apply. Alberta penalties may also apply. Late instalments and unpaid balances accrue prescribed interest, compounded daily. Failure to file T106 may attract penalties generally starting at CAD 25 per day, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Transfer-pricing penalties may equal 10% of the adjustment where the statutory conditions are met. Failure to remit Part XIII tax can create primary corporate liability, interest, penalties, and director exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on taxable dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident, subject to an applicable treaty reduction. Common treaty outcomes include 5% for a qualifying corporate shareholder meeting ownership thresholds and 15% for other qualifying portfolio dividends; the Canada-United States treaty commonly provides 5% for a qualifying 10% corporate owner and 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must establish that the recipient is resident in a treaty country, is the beneficial owner, satisfies applicable limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse conditions, and is entitled to the reduced rate. Obtain and retain CRA Forms NR301 for treaty-eligible beneficial owners, NR302 for partnerships, or NR303 for hybrid entities, or equivalent reliable documentary evidence. A formal recipient tax-residence certificate is not routinely filed with the CRA for each payment, but it should be obtained where needed to substantiate residence. Apply the treaty rate at payment or credit, remit Part XIII tax to the CRA within the applicable deadline, and file NR4 information returns. If entitlement is uncertain, withhold at 25% and seek a refund or competent-authority relief where available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% for interest, royalties, rents, management fees, and similar taxable amounts paid or credited to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Under many Canadian treaties, arm's-length interest is reduced to 10%; the Canada-United States treaty generally eliminates withholding on most arm's-length interest. Royalties commonly have treaty caps of 10%, although rates and covered categories vary; copyright, software, industrial, commercial, scientific, film, equipment, and know-how payments must be classified separately. Related-party interest must also satisfy thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, withholding, and interest-deductibility rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not use a single comprehensive local-file threshold for all transactions. Section 247 of the Income Tax Act requires contemporaneous documentation for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions and the documentation must be prepared by the filing deadline and provided to the CRA within three months of request. T106 reporting generally applies where reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceed the applicable aggregate threshold, commonly CAD 1 million. A transfer-pricing penalty can apply where the net adjustment exceeds the statutory CAD 5 million or 10% of gross revenue tests, subject to the legislation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other reasonable methods supported by reliable facts and economic analysis
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Canadian transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership principles, sham and form-versus-substance doctrines, interest-deductibility rules, and specific anti-avoidance rules can nevertheless deny artificial arrangements. A ULC should maintain Canadian commercial purpose, decision-making evidence, personnel or appropriately documented outsourced functions, premises or operational capability, inventory controls, arm's-length pricing, and records demonstrating actual machinery trading activity. A Canadian ULC may be fiscally transparent for foreign tax purposes only under foreign-law classification; Canadian corporate taxation is not automatically converted to pass-through treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales of excavators, fabricating purchase costs, understating inventory, claiming personal expenses, or knowingly filing materially false T2, AT1, GST/HST, T106, or NR4 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act offences may result in prosecution, fines generally ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, and imprisonment of up to five years. Civil reassessments, gross-negligence penalties, interest, and loss of deductions may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution where they participated, authorized, acquiesced, or wilfully failed to prevent the offence. Directors can also be assessed personally for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST under statutory director-liability rules, subject to due-diligence defences. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty but may arise from criminal process or enforcement orders; imprisonment is possible after conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Remit Payroll, GST/HST, or Part XIII Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using payroll deductions, GST/HST collected, or non-resident withholding tax for operating cash instead of remitting it to the CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Trust-account assessments, prescribed interest, late-remittance penalties, gross-negligence or failure-to-remit penalties, collection action, and prosecution may apply. The corporation may lose access to certificates and face account garnishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST where statutory conditions are met, generally subject to a two-year limitation period after ceasing to be a director and a due-diligence defence. Personal assets may be seized following assessment and collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling used machinery to a foreign affiliate below arm's length, inflating related-party purchase prices, charging unsupported management fees, or using debt and royalties to strip Alberta profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess under section 247, impose transfer-pricing penalties, deny deductions, impute income, assess withholding tax, and apply interest. T106 and contemporaneous-documentation failures create additional penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not ordinarily personally liable solely because of a corporate transfer-pricing reassessment, but personal liability may arise for knowing participation in fraud, statutory remittance failures, or other offences. Civil restitution and criminal sanctions may follow deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity with no beneficial ownership, submitting inaccurate NR301 evidence, or claiming treaty benefits contrary to limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may deny treaty relief, reassess withholding at 25%, impose interest and penalties, and apply the general anti-avoidance rule or treaty anti-abuse provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal exposure for knowingly false certifications, fraudulent withholding practices, or unremitted tax. Ordinary corporate treaty reassessment does not by itself pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an Alberta ULC solely as a conduit while foreign personnel control transactions, invoices, inventory, bank accounts, and pricing, without genuine Canadian operations or records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied under substance, sham, GAAR, transfer-pricing, residence, and treaty principles. The corporation may face reassessment, withholding exposure, interest, penalties, audit escalation, and loss of GST/HST input tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure where they knowingly participate in false records, tax evasion, fraud, or statutory remittance defaults. Veil piercing is exceptional and fact-dependent; criminal conviction can result in fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Proceeds of Crime, and Sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, third-party wire transfers, sanctioned-country payments, dual-use machinery proceeds, falsified bills of lading, or transactions designed to conceal beneficial owners or source of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include FINTRAC compliance measures, suspicious transaction reporting failures, administrative monetary penalties, seizure, forfeiture, prosecution under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and Criminal Code, and sanctions-related offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted for knowing participation, counselling, laundering, sanctions evasion, or obstruction. Convictions can result in substantial fines, forfeiture, imprisonment, and court-imposed conditions including passport surrender or travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain Alberta corporate records, beneficial-ownership information, registers, accounting records, customs documents, or records supporting related-party machinery transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate-law penalties, tax reassessment based on available evidence, denial of deductions or credits, audit compulsion, and offence proceedings may apply. Missing records can shift evidentiary risk materially against the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face offence liability for statutory non-compliance and personal exposure for intentional destruction or falsification of records. Criminal proceedings can generate bail conditions, travel restrictions, fines, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying excavators or rollers, understating customs value, falsifying origin, using incorrect importer-of-record information, or evading duties, GST at importation, or trade controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CBSA reassessment, seizure, forfeiture, monetary penalties under customs legislation, interest, administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can face personal criminal liability for knowing customs fraud or false declarations. Corporate liability is primary for ordinary reassessment, but fraud, obstruction, and conspiratorial conduct can result in fines, imprisonment, forfeiture, and travel restrictions.
